explanation.title: Spanish Reported Speech: Relaying What Others Say

sections.subtitle: Reporting Statements: Present Reporting
sections.content:
💬 REPORTED SPEECH (indirect speech)

Relays what someone said without quoting exactly

Use: DICE QUE (says that) or DIJO QUE (said that)

✅ PRESENT REPORTING

When reporting verb is present (dice que), tenses often stay same

📍 Examples:

DIRECT: Tengo hambre (I'm hungry)
→ REPORTED: Dice que tiene hambre
(He says he's hungry - present stays present)

DIRECT: Voy al cine (I'm going to cinema)
→ REPORTED: Dice que va al cine
(She says she's going to cinema)

DIRECT: He comido (I've eaten)
→ REPORTED: Dice que ha comido
(He says he's eaten - present perfect stays)

💡 Subject pronouns change:
yo → él/ella
nosotros → ellos

📋 PATTERN:
DICE QUE + usually same tenses as original

⚠️ QUE is required in Spanish
(Unlike English where 'that' is often optional)

sections.subtitle: Reporting Statements: Past Reporting & Tense Changes
sections.content:
⏰ PAST REPORTING

When reporting verb is past (dijo que), tenses shift backward

🔄 TENSE BACKSHIFTS:

1️⃣ PRESENT → IMPERFECT
DIRECT: Tengo hambre (I'm hungry)
→ REPORTED: Dijo que tenía hambre
(He said he was hungry)

DIRECT: Estoy cansada (I'm tired)
→ REPORTED: Dijo que estaba cansada
(She said she was tired)

2️⃣ PRETERITE → PLUPERFECT (often)
DIRECT: Comí pizza (I ate pizza)
→ REPORTED: Dijo que había comido pizza
(Said he had eaten pizza)

3️⃣ PRESENT PERFECT → PLUPERFECT
DIRECT: He terminado (I've finished)
→ REPORTED: Dijo que había terminado
(Said he had finished)

4️⃣ FUTURE → CONDITIONAL
DIRECT: Vendré mañana (I'll come tomorrow)
→ REPORTED: Dijo que vendría mañana
(He said he would come tomorrow)

5️⃣ CONDITIONAL → stays CONDITIONAL
Dijo que iría → Dijo que dijo que iría

📋 PATTERN:
DIJO QUE + backshift tenses one step into past

sections.subtitle: Reporting Questions
sections.content:
❓ REPORTED QUESTIONS

Transform direct questions → indirect statements
Remove question marks and adjust word order

✅ YES/NO QUESTIONS

Use SI (if/whether) to introduce:

DIRECT: ¿Tienes hambre? (Are you hungry?)
→ REPORTED: Pregunta si tienes hambre
(He asks if you're hungry)

With past reporting:
→ Me preguntó si tenía hambre
(He asked me if I was hungry - tenía shifts to imperfect)

✅ WH-QUESTIONS

Keep question word, remove question marks:

DIRECT: ¿Dónde vives? (Where do you live?)
→ REPORTED: Pregunta dónde vivo
(He asks where I live)

DIRECT: ¿Qué quieres? (What do you want?)
→ REPORTED: Me preguntó qué quería
(He asked me what I wanted - past, so imperfect)

DIRECT: ¿Cuándo vendrás? (When will you come?)
→ REPORTED: Preguntó cuándo vendría
(He asked when I would come - future → conditional)

📋 PATTERN:
Pregunta/Preguntó + SI (yes/no) or QUESTION WORD + statement order

⚠️ Word order becomes statement order (not inverted)
❌ No question marks in reported questions

sections.subtitle: Reporting Commands & Requests
sections.content:
📢 REPORTED COMMANDS

Use specific verbs + QUE + SUBJUNCTIVE (always!)

💡 Common reporting verbs:
• DECIR (tell)
• PEDIR (ask/request)
• MANDAR (order)
• ROGAR (beg)
• ACONSEJAR (advise)
• ORDENAR (command)
• SUGERIR (suggest)

📋 PATTERN:

Present reporting → present subjunctive
Past reporting → imperfect subjunctive

✅ Examples:

DIRECT: Come la sopa (Eat the soup)
→ PRESENT: Me dice que coma la sopa
(He tells me to eat the soup - present subjunctive)
→ PAST: Me dijo que comiera la sopa
(He told me to eat the soup - imperfect subjunctive)

DIRECT: No hables (Don't talk)
→ Me pide que no hable
(He asks me not to talk - subjunctive)

DIRECT: Estudia más (Study more)
→ Mi madre me dice que estudie más
(My mother tells me to study more)

DIRECT: Ven aquí (Come here)
→ Me dijo que viniera aquí
(He told me to come here)

📍 REQUESTS:
→ Me pidió que le ayudara
(He asked me to help him)

⚠️ Always use subjunctive after these reporting verbs!

sections.subtitle: Time & Place Expression Changes
sections.content:
⏰ TIME & PLACE SHIFTS

When reporting, words shift perspective

🕐 TIME CHANGES (especially with past reporting)

• HOY (today) → ESE DÍA/AQUEL DÍA (that day)
→ Hoy estoy ocupado
→ Dijo que ese día estaba ocupado

• MAÑANA (tomorrow) → AL DÍA SIGUIENTE (next day)
→ Vendré mañana
→ Dijo que vendría al día siguiente

• AYER (yesterday) → EL DÍA ANTERIOR (day before)
→ Ayer fui al cine
→ Dijo que el día anterior había ido al cine

• AHORA (now) → ENTONCES (then)
→ Ahora no puedo
→ Dijo que entonces no podía

• ESTA SEMANA (this week) → ESA SEMANA (that week)

📍 PLACE CHANGES

• AQUÍ/ACÁ (here) → ALLÍ/ALLÁ (there)
→ Estoy aquí
→ Dijo que estaba allí

• ESTE/ESTA (this) → ESE/ESA or AQUEL/AQUELLA (that)
→ Este libro es bueno
→ Dijo que ese libro era bueno

💡 The shift reflects speaker's new perspective and time distance from original statement

sections.subtitle: Sequence of Tenses & Complex Reporting
sections.content:
🔄 SEQUENCE OF TENSES

Maintain logical time relationships when backshifting

📋 When main verb is past, subordinate clauses shift:

→ Sé que María está enferma
(I know María is sick - present knows present)
→ Sabía que María estaba enferma
(I knew María was sick - past knew imperfect)

→ Creo que vendrá
(I think he'll come - present thinks future)
→ Creí que vendría
(I thought he would come - past thought conditional)

📚 MULTIPLE LEVELS

Juan dice: "María dijo que vendría"
→ Juan dice que María dijo que vendría
(Juan says that María said she would come)

🎯 SUBJUNCTIVE IN REPORTED SPEECH

If original uses subjunctive, it stays subjunctive:

→ Quiero que vengas (I want you to come)
→ Dijo que quería que viniera
(He said he wanted me to come)
→ Both shift but remain subjunctive

🔗 MIXING STATEMENTS

Coordinating reported clauses:
→ Me dijo que estaba cansado y que se iría pronto
(He told me he was tired and that he would leave soon)

Use QUE before each clause for clarity

💡 Key: maintain temporal and logical consistency throughout sequence

questions.question: DIRECT: 'Tengo hambre'. REPORTED: 'Dice que ___'

answers.text: tiene hambre (present stays with present reporting)

questions.hint: Present reporting (dice que) usually keeps same tenses. Present → present.

questions.question: DIRECT: 'Estoy cansado'. REPORTED: 'Dijo que ___'

answers.text: estaba cansado (present → imperfect with past reporting)

questions.hint: Past reporting (dijo que) backshifts tenses. Present → imperfect.

questions.question: DIRECT: 'Vendré mañana'. REPORTED: 'Dijo que ___'

answers.text: vendría mañana (future → conditional with past reporting)

questions.hint: Past reporting (dijo que) backshifts. Future → conditional (would come).

questions.question: DIRECT: 'He terminado'. REPORTED: 'Dijo que ___'
questions.hint: Past reporting backshifts. Present perfect → pluperfect (had finished).

questions.question: 'María dice: "Quiero café"'. How to report?
questions.hint: Present reporting keeps tenses. QUE is required: dice QUE quiere.

questions.question: Is QUE required in Spanish reported speech?

answers.text: Yes (dice que, dijo que - que is required)

questions.hint: QUE is required in Spanish: dice QUE, dijo QUE (unlike English where 'that' is optional).

questions.question: DIRECT: '¿Tienes hambre?'. How to report in present?
questions.hint: Yes/No questions use SI (if/whether): Pregunta SI tengo hambre.

questions.question: DIRECT: '¿Dónde vives?'. How to report in present?
questions.hint: Wh-questions keep question word, remove question marks: Pregunta DÓNDE vivo (statement order).

questions.question: DIRECT: '¿Cuándo vendrás?'. REPORTED: 'Me preguntó cuándo ___'
questions.hint: Past reporting question: future → conditional. Asked when I WOULD come.

questions.question: Do reported questions use question marks?

answers.text: No (they become statements: Pregunta dónde vivo)

questions.hint: Reported questions become statements, no question marks: Pregunta dónde vivo (not ¿dónde vivo?).

questions.question: DIRECT COMMAND: 'Come la sopa'. REPORTED: 'Me dice que ___'
questions.hint: Reported commands use subjunctive. Present reporting → present subjunctive: que coma.

questions.question: DIRECT: 'Estudia más'. REPORTED: 'Mi madre me dijo que ___'

answers.text: estudiara más (imperfect subjunctive with past reporting)

questions.hint: Past reporting of commands → imperfect subjunctive: dijo que estudiara.

questions.question: What mood is used for reported commands?
questions.hint: Reported commands ALWAYS use subjunctive: dice que coma, dijo que comiera.

questions.question: 'Me pidió que le ayudara' - What was the original request?
questions.hint: Pidió que + imperfect subjunctive = reported past request. He asked me to help him.

questions.question: ORIGINAL: 'Hoy estoy ocupado'. REPORTED (past): 'Dijo que ___ estaba ocupado'
questions.hint: Time shift with past reporting: HOY (today) → ESE DÍA (that day).

questions.question: ORIGINAL: 'Vendré mañana'. REPORTED (past): 'Dijo que vendría ___'
questions.hint: Time shift: MAÑANA (tomorrow) → AL DÍA SIGUIENTE (the next day).

questions.question: ORIGINAL: 'Ayer fui al cine'. REPORTED (past): 'Dijo que ___ había ido al cine'
questions.hint: Time shift: AYER (yesterday) → EL DÍA ANTERIOR (the day before).

questions.question: ORIGINAL: 'Ahora no puedo'. REPORTED (past): 'Dijo que ___ no podía'
questions.hint: Time shift: AHORA (now) → ENTONCES (then).

questions.question: ORIGINAL: 'Estoy aquí'. REPORTED (past): 'Dijo que estaba ___'
questions.hint: Place shift: AQUÍ (here) → ALLÍ (there) - perspective changes to reporter's location.

questions.question: ORIGINAL: 'Este libro es bueno'. REPORTED (past): 'Dijo que ___ libro era bueno'
questions.hint: Demonstrative shift: ESTE (this) → ESE/AQUEL (that).

questions.question: 'Sé que María está enferma' → 'Sabía que María ___'
questions.hint: Sequence of tenses: main verb past, subordinate shifts accordingly. Knew (past) → was sick (imperfect).

questions.question: 'Creo que vendrá' → 'Creí que ___'
questions.hint: Sequence: main verb past, future shifts to conditional. Thought (past) → would come (conditional).

questions.question: 'Quiero que vengas' → 'Dijo que quería que ___'
questions.hint: Subjunctive in reported speech stays subjunctive but backshifts: vengas → viniera.

questions.question: 'Me dijo que estaba cansado y que ___ pronto' (se iría / se irá)

answers.text: se iría (conditional - maintains past reporting consistency)

questions.hint: Maintain consistency in reported sequence. Both clauses with past reporting use backshifted tenses: estaba (imperfect), se iría (conditional).
